security_audit.summary: The static findings are almost entirely Markdown examples, documented RunComfy CLI usage, expected RunComfy URLs, or documentation shorthand. No prompt injection, covert command execution, or malicious filesystem behavior was found, but the skill does send prompts and media references to a third-party hosted model service.

remediation.suggestion: Tell users not to submit secrets, private briefs, unreleased assets, or sensitive media unless RunComfy processing is approved for that data.
Keep the documented owner-only token file permissions, and recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for ephemeral CI or container use.
Keep commands constrained to the RunComfy CLI with JSON input and avoid adding shell interpolation around user prompts.

content.value_statement: Creative teams need fast image drafts without losing control over prompt structure and model settings. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use RunComfy Flux 2 Klein variants for rapid concepts and polished outputs.
actual_capabilities: Selects the Flux 2 Klein 4B or 9B RunComfy endpoint based on speed or fidelity needs.
Provides RunComfy CLI command patterns for text-to-image generation.
Explains prompt structure for subject, scene, style, lighting, camera, and quality details.
Documents step count, image size, aspect ratio, and reference image limits.
Describes CLI polling, output download behavior, exit codes, and token handling.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication.
Does not generate images locally or provide a self-hosted Flux runtime.
Depends on RunComfy service availability, model limits, and billing behavior.
Embedded text and high-resolution output may require other image models.

use_cases.title: Create fast visual concepts
use_cases.description: Use the 4B variant to explore product, campaign, or illustration ideas with short feedback cycles.

use_cases.title: Polish selected image prompts
use_cases.description: Move a strong concept to the 9B variant with higher step counts for more detail.

use_cases.title: Standardize prompt writing
use_cases.description: Apply the documented subject-first prompt grammar across image generation requests.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux 2 Klein to generate a fast concept image of a modern desk lamp on a clean studio background.

prompt_templates.title: Create a polished product image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux 2 Klein 9B to create a polished product photo of a ceramic mug. Use soft window light, shallow depth of field, and a square output.

prompt_templates.title: Compare fast and final variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me iterate with Flux 2 Klein 4B first, then prepare the final Flux 2 Klein 9B command for the best prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Use reference style guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux 2 Klein with reference images to keep the same lighting and composition while changing the product color and label text.

output_examples.input: Generate a fast concept for a hiking backpack ad.
output_examples.output: A concise RunComfy CLI plan using the Flux 2 Klein 4B endpoint, a subject-first prompt, and a local output directory.

output_examples.input: Make the final image more detailed and ready for review.
output: Keep the prompt under the documented token guidance.
Use dimensions within the aspect ratio and resolution limits.

output_examples.input: Why did my wide poster crop badly?
output_examples.output: An explanation that Flux 2 Klein is capped near 16:9, with a recommendation to revise dimensions or choose a different model.

best_practices: Use the 4B variant for quick exploration and the 9B variant for final polish.
Keep prompts specific, subject-first, and within the documented length guidance.
Use trusted reference image URLs and review generated outputs before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets or private data into image prompts or reference URLs.
Do not request unsupported 4K or extreme aspect ratio outputs from this model.
Do not mix unrelated visual styles across multiple reference images.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI and hosted Flux 2 Klein model endpoints.

faq.question: Which Flux 2 Klein variant should I use first?
faq.answer: Use 4B for fast concepting. Use 9B when you want a more polished final image.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it use reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents support for up to four reference images through the RunComfy endpoint.

faq.question: Is it suitable for precise logo or text rendering?
faq.answer: Not always. The skill recommends other models when embedded text precision is critical.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: You need RunComfy CLI authentication through login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable.
